target: UTM-bundled QEMU, HVF, AArch64 PCI guest, one vCPU, 1 GiB RAM, VirtIO keyboard/tablet and VirtIO sound WAV backend
command: QEMU=build/utm-qemu-probe/qemu-probe QEMU_VIRT='-L /Applications/UTM.app/Contents/Resources/qemu -machine virt,accel=hvf,gic-version=3 -cpu host -smp 1 -m 1024 -device virtio-ramfb -device virtio-keyboard-device -device virtio-tablet-device -audiodev wav,id=sound0,path=build/psalmody-current-b5682-rerun.wav -device virtio-sound-pci,audiodev=sound0' ZEAL_COMPAT_LOG_PATH=build/check-psalmody-current-b5682-rerun.log python3 -u scripts/check-compat.py --pci --quick --probe-psalmody --probe-psalmody-audio-timer
verified: Psalmody opened in the graphical terminal, recording toggled on, and H entered a C note.
QEMU WAV captured a 520 Hz tone in the three 50 ms windows after the leading transition; the note is C5.
Shift+Escape exited playback, the graphical terminal evaluated 40+2 as 42, and zstatus reported failed=0.
The experimental audio timer delivered nine IRQs during the run.
scope_note: This is automated QEMU/WAV evidence for the exact current ISO, not a live UTM audible-output check. The 0.26-second capture includes the generated C5 note but does not establish extended song playback. The user previously reported hearing a Psalmody note through Pi HDMI, but that report was not reproduced against this exact image in this run.
